newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premiums supported by Pakistan, China.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premiums supported by Pakistan, China.

text.p: Substantial buying from Pakistan provided strong support for Thai white sugar while sentiment in the raw sugar market was also lifted on buying from China, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Pakistan has bought at least 10 cargoes of Thai 100 ICUMSA over the past few weeks, including two cargoes ordered last week, they told Reuters.
The price was said to be above the $350 per tonne on CIF basis offered previously by India. Cargill, Kerry and E D & F Man were among the buyers.
"We heard that Pakistan had problems with India on delivery and quality, so it turned to Thailand this time," one trade source said.
The March/April white sugar premiums were quoted at $26 per tonne above London March futures from around $24-25 in the previous week. The white-to-raw premium was about $70 per tonne.
White sugar premiums, also buoyed by big purchases from Indonesia, captured market attention as the raw market struggled for leads.
The vessel Yan Men, chartered by Cargill, was scheduled to leave a Thai port around February 14 to Pakistan with 12,000 tonnes of white sugar, according to shipping sources.

Activity at Thai ports remained dominated by loading of white sugar for Indonesia. At least 286,830 tonnes had been, or would be, delivered to the country between February and early March, shippers said.
On the raw sugar front, traders said a report on China buying had given some relief to the depressed raw market which was in the doldrums before China came in.
"This is a good start. Although the amount is small, it signalled that China will, after all, need to import sugar before the second half of the year," said one trader.
The report had helped lift the raw premiums which have been on a downtrend for some time.
Thai raw premiums for March/May deliveries were bid around 0.20 cents per pound over New York on an FOB basis compared with 0.15-0.25 cents (bid/offer) on Friday.
May/July were quoted at 0.30/0.45 cents per pound over New York on the same basis.

"The impact might not be very strong now. But if there is a sign that the country (China) will buy more, the premiums might shoot up as there are some houses that are running short positions, believing China will not enter the market any time soon," the trader said.
